# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 63 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 47 | Coptic

---

## Saying 63

Jesus said: "There was a rich man who had much money. He said: 'I will put my money to use so that I may sow, reap, plant, and fill my storehouses with produce, so that I will lack nothing.' These were the things he was thinking in his heart. And that night he died. Whoever has ears, let him hear."

---

**Translator's Notes (EMET):**

- Parallel to Luke 12:16-21 (the Parable of the Rich Fool) but Thomas version is shorter, without the divine address
- Thomas omits Luke's "God said to him, 'Fool!'" — the saying ends starkly with death
- **ⲙⲛⲧⲣⲙⲙⲁⲟ** / *mntrmmao*: "rich / richness" — the state of wealth
- "Put my money to use" — Thomas version emphasizes the planning, the endless accumulation strategy
- The conclusion "Whoever has ears, let him hear" marks this as a parable requiring interpretation
